name: Ozzy Osbourne
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Black Sabbath in 1968 and released the band's commercially successful debut album 'Black Sabbath' on 13 February 1970 at age 21, followed by 'Paranoid' (1970) and 'Master of Reality' (1971), all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Osbourne grew up in a working-class family in Aston, Birmingham. He left school at 15 and worked various manual jobs. After hearing the Beatles at 14, he was inspired to become a musician. In late 1967, Geezer Butler recruited him to sing in Rare Breed, which evolved into Polka Tulk Blues, then Earth, and finally Black Sabbath in August 1969. Their debut album, released on Friday 13 February 1970, reached number 8 on the UK Albums Chart and is widely regarded as the first true heavy metal album.
family_context_summary: Osbourne grew up in a small two-bedroom home in Aston, Birmingham. His mother worked at a Lucas factory and his father was a toolmaker at General Electric. The family was working-class with no musical background.
parent_family_domain_summary: No musical or entertainment industry background in the family. Father was a toolmaker, mother a factory worker.
primary_early_advantage_tags: complementary band (Iommi, Butler, Ward), Birmingham music scene, heavy metal wave, working-class adversity
evidence_summary: Osbourne co-founded Black Sabbath at age 19-20 with Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler, and Bill Ward, forming one of the most consequential complementary teams in rock history. The band's debut album (February 1970) and follow-up 'Paranoid' (1970) achieved swift commercial success, riding the emerging heavy metal wave. Osbourne came from a working-class Birmingham family with no music industry connections; his father was a toolmaker and mother a factory worker. He left school at 15, spent time in prison for robbery, and had no formal musical training. The Birmingham industrial environment and the counterculture music explosion of the late 1960s provided the structural wave.

name: Gerd Müller
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1970 Ballon d'Or as European Footballer of the Year and the 1970 FIFA World Cup Golden Boot as top goalscorer with 10 goals, both at age 24-25, well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Müller began his football career at TSV 1861 Nördlingen youth ranks in 1958 at age 12. In 1963, at age 18, he joined Bayern Munich, then in the Regionalliga Süd, where he teamed up with future stars Franz Beckenbauer and Sepp Maier. He scored 33 goals in his first season, helping Bayern earn promotion to the Bundesliga. He became German top scorer multiple times and by 1970 was the most prolific striker in world football, winning the Ballon d'Or on 29 December 1970.
family_context_summary: Müller was born in Nördlingen, Bavaria, the son of Johann Heinrich Müller and Christina Carolina Jung. No significant family financial or football background is documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bayern Munich pipeline, Beckenbauer/Maier teammates, goalscoring instinct, Bundesliga rise
evidence_summary: Müller joined Bayern Munich at 18 and immediately demonstrated extraordinary goalscoring ability, scoring 33 goals in his first season. He benefited from joining Bayern at the start of their rise to European dominance, alongside Franz Beckenbauer and Sepp Maier. By age 25, he had won the 1970 Ballon d'Or and World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals. His family background is poorly documented; no evidence of financial platform or football connections in his family. His unusual physical attributes (short, squat, not notably fast but with lethal acceleration and goalscoring instincts) gave him a distinctive edge that was not conventionally athletic but proved devastatingly effective.

name: Jean-Claude Van Damme
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Karate Championship as a member of the Belgian Karate Team on 26 December 1979 at age 19, and won the Mr. Belgium bodybuilding title in 1978 at age 17-18. Both are material competitive achievements before age 26, though his acting breakthrough came later with Bloodsport (1988) at age 28.
early_history_summary: Van Damme was enrolled by his father in a Shotokan karate school at age 10 in Brussels. He joined the Centre National de Karaté under Claude Goetz at 12, earned a black belt at 18, and compiled a 44-4 semi-contact record from 1976 to 1980. He won Mr. Belgium bodybuilding in 1978 and was on the Belgian team that won the European Karate Championship in December 1979. He opened the California Gym in Brussels in 1979 before moving to the US in 1982 to pursue acting.
family_context_summary: Van Damme was born in Brussels to Eliana and Eugène Van Varenberg, an accountant and florist. His father enrolled him in karate at age 10. The family was middle-class; his father was bilingual and his mother Flemish.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an accountant and florist who enrolled Van Damme in karate school at age 10, supporting his early martial arts training. No direct martial arts or entertainment industry background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Claude Goetz mentorship, karate from age 10, Centre National de Karaté, Belgian Karate Team, Mr. Belgium bodybuilding
evidence_summary: Van Damme's father enrolled him in Shotokan karate at age 10, and he trained under Claude Goetz at the Centre National de Karaté from age 12. This sustained mentorship (6+ years) was the primary early advantage. He earned a black belt at 18, won Mr. Belgium bodybuilding in 1978, and was on the Belgian team that won the European Karate Championship in December 1979. His competitive martial arts achievements by 19 are material but at a national/regional level rather than world-class individually. His acting breakthrough came at 28 with Bloodsport (1988).

name: Aretha Franklin
milestone_by_age_26: Her rendition of 'Respect' reached number one on both the Billboard Hot 100 and R&B charts in June 1967 at age 25, winning two Grammy Awards. She had already been signed to Columbia Records at 18 (1960) and was making $100,000/year by the mid-1960s, all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Franklin began singing solos at New Bethel Baptist Church in Detroit around age 10, where her father C.L. Franklin was a nationally famous preacher. Her father managed her, took her on gospel caravan tours, and helped her sign her first recording deal with J.V.B. Records at 14. At 16, she toured with Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. At 18, she signed with Columbia Records and released her first single 'Today I Sing the Blues' (September 1960), which reached the R&B top 10. After moving to Atlantic Records in 1966, 'Respect' became her first pop chart-topper in June 1967.
family_context_summary: Franklin's father, C.L. Franklin, was a nationally famous Baptist preacher known as the man with the 'million-dollar voice,' earning thousands for sermons. Her mother Barbara was an accomplished piano player and vocalist who died when Aretha was 10. The family home was visited by celebrities including MLK, Sam Cooke, Jackie Wilson, and Clara Ward.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father C.L. Franklin was a nationally renowned Baptist preacher with a 'million-dollar voice' who managed Aretha's early career, took her on gospel caravan tours, and connected her to the music industry. Mother Barbara was an accomplished piano player and vocalist. The household was visited by gospel musicians and civil rights leaders, providing extraordinary domain immersion.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father C.L. Franklin gospel network, New Bethel Baptist Church, MLK/Sam Cooke/Clara Ward access, Detroit music hub, gospel circuit touring, Columbia Records signing
evidence_summary: Franklin's early career was profoundly shaped by her family domain: her father C.L. Franklin was one of the most famous preachers in America, providing access to gospel circuits, celebrity networks (MLK, Sam Cooke, Clara Ward, James Cleveland), and management. She began singing solos at church at 10, recorded at 14, toured nationally at 16, and signed with Columbia Records at 18. By 25, 'Respect' was number one on both pop and R&B charts. Her father's network and the Detroit gospel/church ecosystem provided extraordinary domain proximity and inherited access. Personal adversity (mother's death at 10, pregnancy at 12) coexisted with this platform.

name: Linda Evangelista
milestone_by_age_26: Signed with Elite Model Management and had her first major fashion magazine cover (L'Officiel, November 1984) at age 19. By age 26 (1991), she was one of the most famous supermodels in the world, featured on the cover of British Vogue (January 1990) and in George Michael's 'Freedom! '90' video.
early_history_summary: Evangelista was born to working-class Italian immigrant parents in St. Catharines, Ontario. She attended a modelling school at 12 and entered the Miss Teen Niagara pageant around 1981, where an Elite scout noticed her. She signed with Elite and moved to New York, then Paris, launching her international high-fashion career at 19. Her first major cover was L'Officiel (November 1984). She began working with Karl Lagerfeld and Chanel in 1985, and with photographer Steven Meisel in 1986. Her career breakthrough came in 1988-1989 with the famous short haircut that defined the supermodel era.
family_context_summary: Evangelista was born into a strict working-class Catholic family. Her father Tom worked for General Motors after emigrating from Italy in 1957, and her mother Marisa was a bookkeeper. She was the second of three children.
parent_family_domain_summary: No fashion or entertainment industry connections in the family. Father was a GM factory worker, mother a bookkeeper. Working-class Italian immigrant family with no modelling background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Elite Model Management, Paris fashion world, Karl Lagerfeld muse, Steven Meisel collaboration, supermodel era wave
evidence_summary: Evangelista's early career was driven by institutional ecosystem access: she was scouted by Elite Model Management at a local pageant and moved through the Elite pipeline to New York and Paris. Her first major magazine cover (L'Officiel, November 1984) came at 19. Working with Karl Lagerfeld at Chanel (from 1985) and Steven Meisel (from 1986) accelerated her career. She rode the supermodel wave of the late 1980s-1990s. Her working-class Italian immigrant family provided no fashion industry connections or financial platform; her success was largely self-created through the modelling agency pipeline and her distinctive look.

name: John Lydon
milestone_by_age_26: Became lead vocalist of the Sex Pistols in 1975 at age 19. The band released 'Anarchy in the U.K.' (November 1976), 'God Save the Queen' (May 1977), and the album 'Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols' (28 October 1977) at age 21. He then founded Public Image Ltd in 1978 at age 22, releasing their debut album in 1978.
early_history_summary: Lydon grew up in a working-class Irish immigrant family in north London. He contracted spinal meningitis at age 7, causing hallucinations, memory loss, and a permanent spinal curvature that gave him his distinctive stare. He was expelled from school at 15 and attended Hackney and Kingsway colleges. In 1975, Malcolm McLaren spotted him at the SEX clothing shop due to his ragged look and orange hair, and recruited him as Sex Pistols lead vocalist after he tunelessly sang Alice Cooper's 'I'm Eighteen' on a jukebox.
family_context_summary: Lydon was born to working-class Irish immigrant parents in London. His father worked on building sites and oil rigs. The family lived in a two-room Victorian flat and later a council flat. He was the eldest of four brothers and cared for siblings due to his mother's illnesses.
parent_family_domain_summary: No music industry connections. Father worked in construction and on oil rigs. Working-class Irish immigrant family with no entertainment background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class Irish immigrant, meningitis at 7, London punk scene, Malcolm McLaren's SEX shop, Sex Pistols bandmates, punk rock wave
evidence_summary: Lydon's path was driven by constraint-driven self-creation: working-class Irish immigrant background, spinal meningitis at 7 causing lasting physical and psychological effects, poverty, and no musical training. He was recruited to the Sex Pistols at 19 based on his look and attitude rather than musical skill. The London punk rock wave of 1976-1977 and McLaren's management/scene-building provided the structural context. The complementary team of Sex Pistols (Jones, Cook, Matlock) was crucial. His distinctive 'Lydon stare' resulted from meningitis, turning adversity into a defining visual asset.

name: Zlatan Ibrahimović
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Ajax in July 2001 at age 19-20 and won the 2001-02 Eredivisie title. By age 26 (October 2007), he had also played for Juventus (2004-2006) and Inter Milan (2006-2007), won multiple league titles, been named Serie A Foreign Footballer of the Year (2005), and won the Guldbollen (Swedish player of the year) in 2005.
early_history_summary: Ibrahimović began playing football at age 6 in Malmö, Sweden, alternating between immigrant community clubs FBK Balkan and Malmö BI. He joined Malmö FF youth academy in 1995 at age 13-14 and signed his first contract in 1996. He moved to the senior side in 1999. Ajax signed him in July 2001 for €8.7 million. Under Ronald Koeman, he became a starter and won the 2001-02 Eredivisie title. He scored twice in his Champions League debut in September 2002. He moved to Juventus in 2004 for €16 million and was named Serie A Foreign Footballer of the Year in his first season.
family_context_summary: Ibrahimović was born to a Muslim Bosniak father who emigrated to Sweden in 1977 and a Catholic Croat mother. His parents divorced; at age 9 he was sent to live with his father after his mother was arrested for handling stolen goods. Food was scarce at his father's home; he shoplifted and stole bikes. He grew up in the immigrant-heavy Rosengård area of Malmö.
parent_family_domain_summary: No football background in the family. Father was an immigrant worker; parents divorced. The immigrant community provided access to community football clubs (FBK Balkan, founded by Yugoslav immigrants).
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, divorced parents, immigrant community football, Malmö FF academy, Ajax development, physical dominance, street football skills
evidence_summary: Ibrahimović's early career was shaped by significant adversity: poverty, divorced parents, mother's arrest, hunger, and theft. He used anger as motivation, channeling it into football. He benefited from the Malmö FF youth academy pipeline and the immigrant community football network (FBK Balkan). His exceptional physical attributes (1.95m, athletic, acrobatic) combined with street-football technique gave him a distinctive skill set. Ajax's development ecosystem at age 19-20 accelerated his career, and he won the Eredivisie title in his first season. By 26, he had played for Ajax, Juventus, and Inter Milan, winning multiple league titles and individual awards.

name: Roger Waters
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Pink Floyd in 1965 at age 22 and released the debut album 'The Piper at the Gates of Dawn' on 4 August 1967 at age 23, which reached number 6 on the UK charts. By age 26 (September 1969), Pink Floyd had also released 'A Saucerful of Secrets' (1968) and 'More' (1969), with Waters contributing original songs.
early_history_summary: Waters grew up in Cambridge. His father, a schoolteacher and Communist Party member, was killed in WWII when Roger was 5 months old. He attended Cambridgeshire High School for Boys with Syd Barrett. In 1962, he enrolled at Regent Street Polytechnic School of Architecture in London, where he met Nick Mason and Richard Wright. They began playing music together in late 1963, evolving through several band names before becoming Pink Floyd in 1965. Their debut LP, 'The Piper at the Gates of Dawn,' was released in August 1967 with Waters contributing the song 'Take Up Thy Stethoscope and Walk.'
family_context_summary: Waters was born in Great Bookham, Surrey. His father Eric Fletcher Waters was a schoolteacher, devout Christian, and Communist Party member who was killed at the Battle of Anzio in February 1944 when Roger was 5 months old. His mother Mary was also a teacher. The family moved to Cambridge after his father's death.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a schoolteacher and Communist Party member killed in WWII; mother was also a teacher. No music industry connections. Father's family background was working-class (coal miner's son). The loss of his father became a recurring theme in his work.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Syd Barrett, Nick Mason, Richard Wright, Regent Street Polytechnic, London psychedelic scene, UFO Club, EMI Columbia deal, father killed in WWII
evidence_summary: Waters co-founded Pink Floyd at 22 with Syd Barrett, Nick Mason, and Richard Wright, forming one of rock's most consequential complementary teams. They met at Regent Street Polytechnic School of Architecture, an institutional context that concentrated opportunity. The London psychedelic rock scene of the mid-1960s (UFO Club performances) and EMI Columbia's major label distribution provided the structural wave and native distribution. Waters lost his father in WWII at 5 months old, creating a lifelong theme of loss and urgency. No family music industry connections or financial platform. The Barrett-led debut album (August 1967) reached number 6 on UK charts, with Waters contributing his first sole writing credit.
